findings.where: Hero, first screen at desktop and phone: the headline 'Mark M. Moseley, infrastructure advisor'
findings.fault: The largest words on the page are a name and a generic job title. They are not a line in Mark's own words, and they do not say what he is known for. 'PPP' and 'law' first appear in the smaller sub-line, so the visitor has to read past the headline to learn this is a PPP lawyer and not a general infrastructure consultant.
findings.who_objects: The development-bank official, who is looking for a PPP-law advisor and decides in seconds whether this page is for them. Mark also objects: the brief's client values 3 and 6 ask for him to be heard in his own words through one strong line, and the dualite carry-over is 'a serif headline in Mark's own words'.

findings.where: Hero 'Get in touch' button, and the page as a whole
findings.fault: The only contact route is a button that opens a mailto link. Mark's email address is not shown anywhere on the page. On a managed work machine with no mail client set up, or where the visitor uses webmail, the click does nothing useful, and there is no address to copy.
findings.who_objects: The bank official on a locked-down office laptop, who clicks, gets nothing or an unwanted mail app, and has no address to paste into their own mail. First-visit trust item 7 asks for the full address as its own link text.

findings.where: Article specimen: the pull quote '“Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!”'
findings.fault: Static text is set in the logo blue. The tile's own palette gives that blue to links and the button, and the specimen's real link a few lines below uses the same blue. The quote looks like it might be clickable, and the colour stops meaning 'you can act on this'. It also makes Mark's throwaway quip the loudest line in the article, ahead of his serious point.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles, who sees blue italic text beside a blue link and hovers or clicks it. Angélique, who will copy this style into every post and spread the clash. The text-presentation link rule: a colour that marks links never colours non-link text.

findings.where: Motion sketch (whole sketch) and the hero's first moment
findings.fault: The only element that enters is the heading, and it is all in place within 580 ms with the button already showing. No part of the direction shows the mark being built or gives a quiet moment before the page asks for anything.
findings.who_objects: Mark: client value 2 (calm first, one quiet moment before any text asks) and value 7 (the logo is built by the opening animation) apply to every direction, and this direction answers neither.

findings.where: Hero sub-line: 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience'
findings.fault: In the most prominent proof spot, standing is claimed with a size word (a count of years) and not shown through checkable work: no regions, bodies or kinds of work beyond the one World Bank role.
findings.who_objects: A procurement-minded official who selects advisors against terms of reference. They look for the kinds of projects and regions Mark has worked on, and a years count does not tell them that ('Feel the CV': checkable specifics, never size words; item 6, regions of work).

findings.where: Page as a whole: no third-party proof
findings.fault: There is no outside proof anywhere: no links to work that named bodies host, no publications by named institutions. The only proof is a self-stated former role.
findings.who_objects: The bank official, who wants to see that organisations like theirs have used or published Mark's work before getting in touch (first-visit trust item 14: with no testimonials held, link out to work that named bodies host).

findings.fault: This heading is set in large Source Sans semibold, while the tile's own type pair says Source Sans is for the nav, buttons, labels and dates only, and Gelasio is for headings. The tile breaks its own rule within a few lines of stating it.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds, and Angélique, who would copy the tile and not know which face a heading takes.

findings.where: Style-tile section labels: 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' (right column) against 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' (left column)
findings.fault: The same small section label is drawn two ways: with a hairline rule under it in the right column, and without one in the left. Two looks for one kind of part make the grouping read as inconsistent.
findings.who_objects: A designer or editor reusing the tile, who cannot tell whether a section label takes a rule.

findings.where: Header at phone width (390 px): the logo lockup
findings.fault: At phone width the header shows only the arches and 'MMM INFRA', dropping 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services'. This cut-down version of the logo is not one the brand sheet lists, so it has not been cleared with the client.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo per brand sheet §4 sets the full name to the right. A phone visitor arriving on an article page, who would see only an acronym as the site's name.

findings.where: Hero at phone width: the portrait stand-in panel below the button
findings.fault: The mist panel starts about 108 px in from the left and runs to the right edge. It is out of line with the text column above it, so it reads as a box that has slipped.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor scrolling the first screen, who sees a misaligned grey block where a photograph of Mark should anchor the page.
